strengths: Insightful analysis of the failure modes in native text-to-3D latent spaces: The paper characterizes the 'sink trap' phenomenon and expressivity mismatch between textual conditioning and geometric capacity in native 3D generative models (e.g., TRELLIS), supported by quantitative diversity ratio analysis ($R = \Delta_{vis}/\Delta_{text}$) and velocity norm profiling.

A simple, effective, and training-free inversion strategy: By discarding the approximate source prompt and conducting inversion unconditionally with empty prompts before running null-text optimization, the method effectively avoids trajectory instability and latent explosion on out-of-distribution shapes.

Efficient and native 3D manipulation: Unlike prior 3D editing approaches that rely heavily on 2D diffusion distillation (SDS), multi-view rendering loops, or 2D inpainting backbones (e.g., Flux/Gemini), this framework operates purely within the native 3D latent space, running roughly 20x faster than baselines like VoxHammer while preventing geometric collapse.

Convincing qualitative retargeting on challenging non-rigid benchmarks: The paper demonstrates impressive pose-preserving retargeting across diverse semantic character classes on out-of-distribution meshes from the DT4D dataset.
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: The technical approach is largely a direct application of forward Euler inversion with empty prompt conditioning combined with standard Null-Text Inversion (NTI) optimization (Mokady et al., 2023) applied to TRELLIS's structure model ($G_S$). The contribution is primarily an empirical diagnostic and practical observation rather than a new generative or inversion formulation.

Single 3D backbone evaluation: The empirical study and validation are conducted exclusively on TRELLIS. While TRELLIS is representative of open-source native text-to-3D models, experimenting with only one model makes it difficult to assess whether 'sink traps' and extreme velocity divergence under approximate prompts are universal across native 3D generative architectures or largely artifacts of TRELLIS's specific training dataset and sparse structure latent space.

Scope of editing is predominantly pose retargeting: The evaluated editing tasks are almost entirely whole-body character retargeting (e.g., transforming a humanoid/animal into another character in the same pose). Localized edits (e.g., adding/modifying an object part, partial editing) and geometric edits preserving subtle surface geometry are not extensively explored, partly due to the coarse $64^3$ resolution of the structure model.

Ambiguity regarding findings across 2D vs. 3D models: Section 4.2 argues that 3D models are uniquely vulnerable to prompt mismatch compared to 2D models, yet Table 5 in the supplementary shows that using an empty prompt also significantly improves inversion PSNR over ground-truth prompts in Stable Diffusion v1.4 (from 15.73 to 22.79 on COCO). The paper should clarify more clearly which aspects of unconditional inversion are specific to 3D geometry versus general properties of classifier-free guidance inversion.

strengths: Timely and relevant exploration into the latent inversion and editing capabilities of native text-to-3D generative models, an area that remains less explored than 2D diffusion inversion.

Insightful analysis of the 'sink trap' phenomenon and text-conditioning sensitivity, showing how approximate text prompts cause significant drift in velocity norms and fail to invert non-rigid 3D shapes.
Operating entirely natively in 3D latent space bypasses expensive multi-view rendering and 2D inpainting steps, yielding substantial computational speedups (approx. 20x faster than VoxHammer).
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: The technical approach consists almost entirely of applying standard forward Euler inversion and Null-Text Inversion (NTI) using an empty prompt to the first stage of the pre-trained TRELLIS backbone. While the empirical observation is intriguing, the methodological formulation introduces minimal new mechanics or theoretical formulations beyond existing 2D inversion literature.

Evaluation restricted to a single 3D generative backbone: All 3D experiments and empirical claims rely strictly on TRELLIS. It is unclear whether the 'sink trap' and the severe sensitivity to approximate prompts are universal properties of text-to-3D models or specific artifacts of TRELLIS's sparse structure flow, latent representation, and training distribution. Validation on additional native 3D generative architectures (e.g., Shap-E or other diffusion/flow-based 3D models) is necessary to substantiate the general claims.

Narrow scope of edits: The demonstrated edits are largely restricted to character/animal pose retargeting (e.g., re-skinning an existing humanoid or quadruped pose into another persona). The paper does not demonstrate whether this inversion technique can handle localized structural modifications, additive/subtractive edits, or non-articulated man-made objects.

Insufficient evaluation and baselines: Quantitative evaluation of editing (Table 3) is limited to a single multi-view SigLIP score against only two baselines (native TRELLIS stage-2 and VoxHammer). Key aspects such as structural preservation versus edit faithfulness are not quantified with geometric metrics (e.g., Chamfer Distance, normal consistency) or a rigorous user study. Comparisons against other recent 3D editing methods mentioned in related work (e.g., 3D-LATTE, Nano3D) are missing.

Ambiguity regarding the distinction between 2D and 3D inversion: In Section F and Table 5, the authors report that inverting Stable Diffusion v1.4 without a prompt on COCO and DiffusionDB also yields significantly higher PSNR and better LPIPS than using ground-truth prompts. This observation partially undermines the core narrative of the paper that 3D models exhibit a fundamentally distinct failure mode compared to 2D models, suggesting instead that null-prompt Euler/NTI inversion may simply be an inherent consequence of classifier-free guidance dynamics across diffusion/flow models.

strengths: Insightful Characterization of Native 3D Latents: The paper identifies and analyzes an important phenomenon in native text-to-3D models ('sink traps'), clearly illustrating the severe mismatch between geometric representational capacity and text-conditioning sensitivity.

Bypassing the Source Prompt Requirement: While conventional inversion (e.g., NTI in 2D) relies on a faithful or approximate source prompt, the paper convincingly demonstrates that approximate prompts in 3D cause severe trajectory drift (high velocity norms). Using an empty prompt effectively stabilizes inversion trajectories and avoids out-of-distribution drift.

Fully Native and Fast 3D Pipeline: Unlike existing methods that depend heavily on 2D inpainting, multi-view rendering, or expensive score distillation, the proposed pipeline operates purely within the native 3D flow latent space, achieving ~20x faster runtime compared to baselines like VoxHammer.

Comprehensive Empirical Diagnostics: The paper backs up its claims through thoughtful analyses, including the diversity ratio R, inversion velocity norms across timesteps, and comparisons with 2D generative models (FLUX, SD-v1.4).
weaknesses: Modest Algorithmic Novelty: Algorithmically, the approach is essentially the forward Euler inversion and Null-Text Optimization (NTI) adapted to Rectified Flow, with the source prompt set to null (empty prompt). The primary contribution is the empirical finding and practical adaptation rather than a novel inversion algorithm.

Generalizability Across 3D Backbones: The empirical findings and validation are conducted exclusively on TRELLIS. While TRELLIS is the leading open-source native text-to-3D model, it remains unclear whether the 'sink trap' phenomenon and the effectiveness of unconditional inversion are fundamental properties of native 3D generative architectures or specific to TRELLIS's training data distribution and conditioning mechanisms.

Scope of Shape Editing: The demonstrated editing capabilities primarily focus on character/global retargeting (preserving the pose/silhouette while altering semantic category) rather than localized geometric edits (e.g., adding an accessory, selective deformation, or fine-grained part modifications).

Nuance in the 2D vs. 3D Comparison: In the main text, the authors suggest that 2D models are robust to approximate prompts whereas 3D models uniquely fail. However, Section F and Table 5 in the appendix show that empty prompt inversion also improves reconstruction quality in 2D image models (Stable Diffusion), which slightly weakens the claim that this failure mode is uniquely distinctive to 3D generative priors.

strengths: Insightful diagnostic and empirical analysis: The paper identifies and analyzes the 'sink trap' phenomenon and velocity norm instabilities during inversion in native text-to-3D rectified flow models (e.g., TRELLIS), highlighting the expressivity mismatch between textual conditioning and 3D geometric capacity.

Simplicity and efficiency of the proposed fix: Using an empty/null prompt during Euler inversion combined with null-text optimization effectively stabilizes trajectories and bypasses out-of-distribution text guidance without requiring retraining, 2D inpainting backbones, or costly per-scene SDS optimization.
Strong performance on challenging non-rigid poses: Demonstrates high-fidelity inversion and character retargeting on non-rigid poses from DT4D where standard prompt-conditioned baselines struggle.
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: The proposed framework directly combines forward Euler inversion with an empty prompt and Null-Text Inversion (NTI, Mokady et al., 2023) adapted to flow models. The technical novelty lies predominantly in the empirical observation rather than an algorithmic innovation.

Contradictory claims regarding 2D vs. 3D behavior: The main text argues that 3D models suffer uniquely from prompt mismatch compared to 2D models where 'any reasonable prompt works' (Sec. 4.2). However, Supplementary Section F and Table 5 reveal that inverting without a prompt also dramatically improves reconstruction over ground-truth prompts in Stable Diffusion v1.4 (PSNR 22.79 vs. 15.73 on COCO). This undermines the central claim that this phenomenon and solution are uniquely tied to the 3D domain.

Narrow scope of editing capabilities: The editing demonstrations (Figs. 6, 7, 11, 12) are almost entirely restricted to whole-body character retargeting/reskinning (e.g., human pose to clown, astronaut, pirate). The paper does not demonstrate fine-grained, localized, or non-retargeting edits (e.g., adding an accessory, modifying localized parts).

Evaluation clarity and baseline handling: In Section 5.3, VoxHammer is reported to fail on 67% of DT4D samples due to latent value explosion, but it is unclear how these failed samples were handled when computing the quantitative scores in Table 3. Furthermore, visual figures (e.g., Figs. 2, 6, 8, 11, 16) are rendered quite small, making it difficult to assess fine surface geometry and mesh quality.

strengths: Insightful analysis of 'sink traps' in text-to-3D models: The paper provides a compelling empirical analysis revealing that native 3D generative models suffer from a severe mismatch between geometric expressivity and linguistic sensitivity, leading to trajectory instability when using approximate text prompts.

Simple yet effective solution: Recognizing that the unconditional prior avoids out-of-distribution drift and enables stable Euler/null-text inversion of complex, arbitrary 3D shapes is an elegant and practical finding.

Native 3D editing efficiency: By avoiding auxiliary 2D inpainting networks, multi-view SDS, or manual masking, the proposed pipeline operates natively in 3D latent space in roughly 9 seconds per edit, orders of magnitude faster than optimization-heavy methods like Vox-E.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The authors evaluate multiple 3D generative architectures (TRELLIS, LN3Diff, GaussianAnything) and compare against 2D diffusion behavior (SD, FLUX), supported by diverse metrics (latent L1, normal LPIPS, CLIP, SigLIP, and VLM evaluations) on non-rigid DT4D meshes.
weaknesses: Algorithmic novelty is somewhat limited: The core technical mechanism directly ports Null-Text Inversion (NTI) to rectified flow models using an empty prompt. While the empirical diagnosis of why this works in 3D is valuable, the algorithmic formulation is largely an adaptation of established 2D techniques.

Editing scope primarily restricted to pose-preserving retargeting: The showcased edits primarily focus on re-skinning or retargeting character identity/clothing while preserving the underlying pose. The ability to perform more flexible structural changes (e.g., adding/removing parts or changing topology) remains limited.

Mathematical clarity in Algorithm 1 and CFG formulation: The editing step at the bottom of Algorithm 1 lacks explicit equations detailing how the target prompt $P_{\text{edit}}$, the optimized unconditional embeddings $\{e^{(i)}_{\text{uncond}}\}$, and the guidance weight $\omega$ are combined during the editing generation pass.

Surface detail and geometry resolution: The reconstructed and edited meshes exhibit noticeable surface artifacts and voxelization roughness inherent to the TRELLIS structure latent space, occasionally affecting geometric crispness.

strengths: Timely and well-motivated problem: while inversion and latent-space editing are mature in 2D diffusion and flow models, systematically studying inversion and editing inside native 3D generative backbones (such as TRELLIS) is novel and important.

Insightful analysis of the 'sink trap' phenomenon and text-geometry expressivity mismatch: the empirical analysis (using the diversity ratio R and velocity norms in Figures 2/4 and Tables 1/2) convincingly shows that native 3D models suffer much more severely from out-of-distribution textual conditioning during inversion than their 2D counterparts.

Simple, training-free, and effective solution: using unconditional forward inversion combined with null-text optimization avoids OOD guidance instabilities and yields high-fidelity 3D reconstructions.

Significant efficiency gain over prior 3D editing pipelines: by performing inversion and editing natively in the 3D latent space, the method avoids expensive per-scene SDS optimization (e.g., Vox-E) and multi-view 2D rendering/inpainting iterations (e.g., VoxHammer), running in ~9 seconds per edit.
weaknesses: Methodological novelty is relatively limited: the core technical approach directly adapts Euler inversion and Null-Text Inversion (NTI) to rectified flow 3D models, where the primary operational change is setting the inversion condition to the empty string.

Evaluation lacks explicit quantitative metrics for structure/pose preservation during editing: Table 3 only measures text-image alignment (SigLIP, CLIP, VLM scores), without complementary geometric distance metrics (e.g., Chamfer distance, keypoint/pose alignment, or normal consistency) to quantify how well the source pose/structure is preserved versus distorted.

Restricted editing scope: the demonstrated editing capability is mostly restricted to full-body character retargeting / semantic replacement (e.g., modifying an entire character into a cowboy, astronaut, or duck while retaining pose). Localized, fine-grained geometric additions or removals (e.g., adding an accessory or modifying an isolated part) are not demonstrated.

Minor cross-referencing and figure errors: on page 12, the text references 'visual comparisons in Supp. Fig. 7' (which seems to refer to Supp. Fig. 16), and cites 'Supp. Mat. (Table 1)' for DT4D reconstruction results (which appears as Table 4 in the supplement).
